findings.claim: init-templates.ts:3005-3010: "an unterminated fence runs to the end of the file. A floor marker quoted inside a fence is prose about the marker, never the marker"; changeset line 5: "markers quoted inside a fenced code block are prose and never pair"; eject.ts:729 comment "A marker quoted inside a fenced code block is prose, not a block."
findings.counterexample:
OBSERVED, and it is a REGRESSION introduced by this fold. `fencedRanges` closes an unterminated opener at EOF (init-templates.ts:3024), so ONE unbalanced fence line at <=3-space indent anywhere above the span makes the REAL span prose. Input `# Mine

```sh
echo hi

<START>
blk
<END>
tail
`: post-fold `locateAgentsFloorSpan` -> null, `totem eject` -> `summary.skipped = ['AGENTS.md (no Totem block)']` with the entire managed Totem span still in the file, and `totem init` -> `{action:'preserved', err:'AGENTS.md is yours (no `<!-- totem:agents-floor:start -->` … `<!-- totem:agents-floor:end -->` span) — left untouched; add the two marker lines…'}` while both marker lines are present — the floor silently stops being refreshed, permanently. The pre-fold locator at d949abb6 returns `{start:23,end:92}` on the identical input (scratchpad/old.mjs, both functions run side by side). Four independent ways to reach it, all OBSERVED (scratchpad/c2.mjs, c5.mjs): a ```-opened block closed with ~~~ (F2, CommonMark agrees it does not close), a lone stray fence (F4), a fence inside an HTML comment (F5 — CommonMark says the ``` inside an HTML block is NOT a fence, so here the code diverges and invents the range), and a 4-space-indented opener whose closer is at column 0 (I3). Worse, with a lone fence BETWEEN two spans (F10) eject removes the first span, leaves the second COMPLETE canonical span untouched, and reports `{"scrubbed":["AGENTS.md"]}` — clean, over a surviving Totem block, falsifying "removes every complete span" with no residue line. Cheap remedy: treat only CLOSED fences as prose ranges (drop the `if (open !== null)` tail at 3024) — every quoted-marker case the fold set out to fix (their own tests at init.test.ts:4426/4440, eject.test.ts:437) uses a closed fence and would still pass. This repository's own AGENTS.md is unaffected today (0 fence lines, `grep -c '^\s*```' AGENTS.md` = 0).

findings.claim: G5's fold: "The line terminator is read from the bytes OUTSIDE the span: the span is about to be replaced, so its own endings must not decide the file's" (init.ts:794-795; eject.ts:752-754). Changeset line 5: "in the line terminator the rest of the file uses".
findings.counterexample:
OBSERVED, two residues. (1) "Outside" is whole-file-minus-THIS-span, so a SECOND span's endings still decide the first seam: `# Mine

<LF span>

mid

<CRLF span>
tail
` scrubs to `"# Mine

mid
tail
"` — two CRLFs injected into a region that was pure LF, and the injection then propagates into the second seam's `detectEol` (scratchpad/c3.mjs E3). Init does the same: the LF span is refreshed to CRLF because the other span carries CRLF (E3i). (2) When the outside carries no terminator at all, `detectEol('')` returns LF (init-templates.ts:2995 "CRLF when it carries any"), so a file that is nothing but a CRLF span with no trailing newline is rewritten by init to a pure-LF file — a byte no-op before this fold, `{action:'refreshed'}` now (c3.mjs E1bi; the trailing-CRLF variant E1ci is correctly `unchanged`). Both are narrower than G5's original and converge in one write; the core G5 shape (span is the file's only CRLF source) is genuinely cured (c3.mjs E4 -> `# Mine

intro

## Rules
`, no CR).

findings.claim: [NOTE] G12's fold: `existsExact` in the script "Mirrors the sterility test's `existsExact`" (tools/public-refs-resolve.mjs:100-103).
findings.counterexample: OBSERVED, correct on this host but not a mirror. Case-exact true/false answers on NTFS (`…/AGENTS.md` true, `…/agents.md` false while existsSync is true; `C:/Windows/win.ini` true, `WIN.INI` false), and it terminates correctly on a Windows drive root (`path.parse` root `D:\`; `D:/` and `D:` both true) and on a UNC root. The difference from the test's copy (agents-floor-sterility.test.ts:110-112) is the missing containment guard `if (relative.startsWith('..') || path.isAbsolute(relative)) return false` — the script has no ROOT, so a link that escapes the repository resolves on disk: fixture `[up](../exists.md)` -> `OK … -> exists` while the offline half would FAIL the same link as missing. Also the header (lines 18-19) still says only "checked on disk" and never says the check is now case-exact, which is the one behaviour change a runner would want named.

verdict: Shape by shape against the previous leg's twelve. G1's exact two-orphan and nested mutants are removed WITHIN one invocation (both user texts survive, residue named — reproduced against dist), and the forward cursor could not be defeated by construction — but the property is invocation-scoped, and a second totem eject, or one totem init, on the residue destroys exactly what run 1 preserved and reports clean (H1). G2 is cured. G5's core is cured and two narrower residues remain (H4). G3's three shapes and G4's libuv exit-127 are cured — live run 8/8, EXIT=0 — with a sibling over-extraction unfixed (H5); G12's existsExact is correct including drive-root and UNC, with the containment asymmetry still open (H8). G6 is cured as claimed, minus three all-caps/period forms and a now-false docstring adjective (H7). G7, G8, G9 and G11's init half are answered; the committed span is independently byte-identical to AGENTS_FLOOR_BLOCK (1882/1882, pure LF) and the eject-side prose was not brought forward (H6). G10 is the one where the fix bought a worse bug than it sold: fenced quotation is now prose, but an unbalanced fence makes a REAL span prose, so eject leaves the whole Totem block behind saying (no Totem block) and init tells the user to add marker lines that are already there, a regression against d949abb6 (H2); and the two uncovered quoting forms still delete user prose with a clean report (H3). This fold has NOT converged: three MATERIAL survive (H1, H2, H3) plus H5 at the calibration the previous leg set for the identical class. None is BLOCKING — nothing misbehaves on this repository's own surfaces today (AGENTS.md carries no fences, no inline marker quotation, one span, LF) — and H2 has a one-line conservative remedy that keeps every test the fold added green. [Seat's fold, appended: all eight folded in the commit that follows 1825a3cd — only closed fences are prose and a marker counts only as a whole line (H2, H3), the terminator falls back to the file's own when nothing outside the span carries one (H4, the multi-span mixed-EOL case disclosed in the helper's docstring as a broken file), the stray-marker hints on both sides say that a start followed by an end is a span by definition and the docs state the contract (H1, H6 — the ambiguity itself is not decidable by the tool and is answered by fewer accidental markers plus the loud hint), the script skips footnotes and prose-shaped definitions, fails links that escape the working directory and names the case-exact check (H5, H8), and the Proposal pattern takes the all-caps forms with the docstring corrected (H7).]
